newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TORONTO, FLYERS WIN, BRUINS TIE WHALERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TORONTO, FLYERS WIN, BRUINS TIE WHALERS.

text.p: Rick Tocchet scored his second goal of the game with less than three minutes left in regulation to lift the Boston Bruins to a 4-4 tie with the Hartford Whalers on Thursday.

Tocchet tied it at 4-4 with his sixth goal of the season at 17:06 of the third period when he put the rebound of a shot by Steve Staios past Jason Muzzatti's glove side. Muzzati misplayed the fluttering puck and allowed Tocchet to poke the puck home.
"In San Jose, we were down 3-0 and we came back, it's nice to know you can do that once in a while when you're behind," said Tocchet. "You don't want to do it too often, but you can do it."
Bill Ranford made 33 saves for Boston.
At the Islanders, Mike Craig, Sergei Berezin and Doug Gilmour each scored in a 5:36 span of the second period to rally the Toronto Maple Leafs to a 5-3 victory over the listless New York Islanders.
Zigmund Palffy scored twice in a 49-second span to give the Islanders a 2-1 lead, but Toronto coach Mike Murphy called a timeout and the Maple Leafs rallied for three goals in the next six minutes.
Toronto took the lead for good with 8:08 left in the period on Berezin's second goal.
At Tampa Bay, Trent Klatt scored twice in the first six minutes of the third period as the Philadelphia Flyers rallied with four goals to beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 4-3.
The Lightning exploded for a 3-0 lead in the first 13:19 of the game on goals by Brian Bradley, Dino Ciccarelli and Brian Bellows.
But Mikael Renberg got the Flyers on the board with 4:18 left in the second period and Scott Daniels made it a one-goal game 95 seconds later, setting up Klatt's heroics.
Ron Hextall made 25 saves for the Flyers.
